intro:
This guide covers {pubCount} open Wetherspoons pubs in Derby across {areaCount} areas: Iron Gate and Babington Lane. Every pub works from the national [Wetherspoons menu](/), but prices are set locally. Use it to choose between The Standing Order, The Thomas Leaper and The Babington Arms, then check the menu and typical prices at your chosen pub.

The guide also explains breakfast timings, club days and ordering options, with practical advice on what to confirm before visiting.

The Babington Arms is the listed Wetherspoons on Babington Lane. It suits visitors whose plans already bring them to this area, without needing to choose between the Iron Gate pubs. Check its own menu for current dishes and typical prices before ordering.

pricing:
Wetherspoons menu prices in Derby are set pub by pub, even though the food menu is broadly the same nationally. Treat any guide price as typical, not as the amount every local pub will charge.

Popular dishes on the national menu include [burgers](/burgers), curries, fish and chips and pizza. Check the selected pub's menu to see what is offered and how each option is priced.

Central locations can matter: city centre pubs often charge more than suburban pubs. That does not establish which Derby pub is cheapest. For the exact current price, check the menu at your chosen pub or select that pub in the Wetherspoon app before placing an order.
breakfastAndClubs:
Breakfast at Wetherspoons is typically served from eight in the morning until noon, but confirm the service times at your chosen Derby pub. The traditional breakfast is among the popular dishes on the national menu; check the local menu before planning your order.

[Curry Club](/curry-club) is traditionally on Thursday and [Steak Club](/steak-club) on Tuesday at participating pubs. Do not assume that every listed pub participates or has identical club details. Ask The Standing Order, The Thomas Leaper or The Babington Arms about the relevant day, current menu and typical prices before making it the basis of your visit.
